formulas.name: Pure state condition
formulas.when_to_use: To check if a quantum state represented by a density matrix is pure.

formulas.name: Mixed state condition
formulas.when_to_use: To determine if a quantum state is a statistical mixture of states.
assumptions: ρ is a valid density operator

formulas.name: Expectation value (density operator)
formulas.when_to_use: To calculate the average outcome of measuring an observable A on state ρ.
common_mistakes: Using ρA instead of its trace

sections.title: Mixing and states of composite systems

concepts.definition: Preparation of |0⟩ or |1⟩ with probability 1/2 each; not equivalent to coherent superposition |+⟩.
Classical random preparation of normalized pure states |ψ_j⟩ with probabilities p_j.
tr(UAU†) = tr(A). The trace is basis-independent.
tr(AB) = tr(BA). Note: the PDF appears to repeat AB on both sides in Eq. (4.8).

concepts.front: Hermiticity of a pure-state density operator
Density operator of a mixed ensemble

concepts.definition: Pure iff tr(ρ²) = 1; mixed if tr(ρ²) < 1. The script’s Eq. (4.31) prints tr(ρ)=1, apparently a typo.

concepts.front: Equal mixture of computational basis states

concepts.definition: Different ensembles Σ_j p_j|ψ_j⟩⟨ψ_j| and Σ_k q_k|φ_k⟩⟨φ_k| can define the same ρ.
Equal density operators give equal observable expectations: ⟨A⟩ = tr(Aρ).
A density operator generally does not single out one privileged underlying pure-state ensemble.
ρ_k = π_k ρ π_k / p_k, for p_k > 0.
ρ_A = tr_B(ρ) is the state of subsystem A after disregarding B.
A⊗I acts on subsystem A and leaves B unchanged.
A pure composite state that is not a product state; its reduced states are mixed.

workbook_source_caveats.note: Professor Jens Eisert, Chapter 4: Density operators, uploaded QMChapter4(2).pdf
Only material in the uploaded Chapter 4 lecture script. Existing learning-card explanations preserved.
PDF prints tr(AB)=tr(AB) while the surrounding text calls it cyclic interchange. LaTeX uses tr(AB)=tr(BA) and flags this as a correction.
PDF prints tr(ρ)=1 for pure states, but surrounding text establishes tr(ρ²)=1. LaTeX uses tr(ρ²)=1 and flags the misprint.
LaTeX uses the script’s abbreviated partial-trace notation Σ_j ⟨j|ρ|j⟩; bra/ket act on subsystem B.
Telegram Bot API does not natively typeset LaTeX. Render to image with KaTeX/MathJax or another TeX renderer. The HTML column is escaped code display, not a rendered formula.
Post-measurement formula applies for outcomes with nonzero probability p_k.
Named concepts and important formulas selected from lecture; not every selected formula is literally in a boxed callout in the PDF.
